clue.text: Old liner is able to get carrier by radio

parts.note: to be able to do something is to be able, so 'can'

indicators.note: something heard by radio is only heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a bearer is one who carries something

explanation.surface: An old ocean liner manages to receive a signal from an aircraft carrier over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by radio' signals a sound-alike: BEARER said in a non-rhotic accent gives BERRA, though the match is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canberra was a P&O passenger ship, retired in 1997, so a liner of the past.

clue.text: 8 is under grit spreader

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece written under another comes after it
a grit spreader scatters its load, so the letters of the word grit are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A river is beneath the vehicle spreading grit on an icy road.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' points to the answer of 8 down, a river; the down-clue convention puts IS after TIGR, the rearranged GRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tigris is a great river of Mesopotamia, flowing through Turkey and Iraq, so it is a water runner.

clue.text: 8 firm ushers in lots of real trouble

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: an usher walks in front, so the front letters of the next words are taken

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble, as in 'much ado'

explanation.surface: A company starts a great deal of genuine bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ushers in' signals the opening letters L, O and R of 'lots of real'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colorado is the river that carved the Grand Canyon, so a watercourse of the American West.

clue.text: Stamped out first sign of megalomania in former Prime Minister

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Ted Heath was British Prime Minister from 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: A power-mad former Prime Minister crushed the earliest hint of his own megalomania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stamped out' looks like 'suppressed' but is the definition: coins are stamped out. TED is Edward Heath, a British Prime Minister of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins are minted by being struck or pressed from metal blanks, a synonym in the coining sense.

clue.text: Angela's supporter, backing the Queen, briefly

definitions.note: the surname belonging to Angela, the girls' school-story writer

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Liz is a short form of Elizabeth, the Queen's name

explanation.surface: A woman's undergarment, backing the Queen, is mentioned in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: Angela Brazil (1868-1947) wrote school stories for girls, so 'Angela's' stands for her surname; the underwear surface hides this.
explanation.definitionFit: Angela Brazil was a popular British author of girls' boarding-school stories, so her family name completes the possessive.

clue.text: Limits us in Bond novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A spy story restricts the reader to us in a Bond book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a James Bond book but is the anagram signal for US and BOND together.
explanation.definitionFit: Bounds are boundaries or limits, as in 'out of bounds', an exact plural synonym.

clue.text: In a very short time, girl to be quiet

definitions.note: in as an adjective meaning fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

parts.note: mo is short for moment, as in 'half a mo'
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
sh is the call to be quiet

explanation.surface: Within moments, a girl is told to keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a preposition opening the sentence but is the definition, meaning fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in is fashionable, and modish means fashionable too, a pair of synonyms.

clue.text: He takes care of one to shrug away from violation of human rights

indicators.note: a violation breaks something apart, so the letters of the phrase are broken and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of shrug are the ones taken away

explanation.surface: A man looks after someone, refusing to shrug off abuses of human rights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to shrug away from' takes S, H, R, U, G out of the letters of HUMAN RIGHTS, and 'violation of' rearranges the six left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract killer 'takes care of' a target, a gangland euphemism for killing someone.

clue.text: Runner, with broken right toe, a curse

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: An athlete, with a broken right toe, utters a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, which the broken toe supports, but it means something that runs: a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Water runs along a river or stream, so a runner is a crossword-style name for a flowing channel.

clue.text: 8 doubt expressed before using most of federal capital

parts.note: to hum and haw is to express doubt or hesitation

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter

parts.note: Bern is the federal capital of Switzerland

explanation.surface: Hesitation is voiced before spending nearly all of a nation's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' points to the answer of 8 down. BERN, Switzerland's federal city, loses its last letter to give BER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Humber is a large tidal estuary in eastern England, fed by the Trent and Ouse.

clue.text: Renegade postgraduate reformed, no longer taking drug

indicators.note: something reformed is formed again, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the letters of drug are the ones dropped

explanation.surface: A rebellious graduate student cleans up and gives up drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no longer taking drug' removes D, R, U, G from POSTGRADUATE; 'reformed' rearranges the eight letters left over.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or faith, which is what an apostate does with a religion, a near synonym.

clue.text: 8 to end socialist setback

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter
set back means turned backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: red is a common term for a socialist or communist

explanation.surface: A river puts an end to a socialist's setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to end' gives the last letter O of 'to'; 'setback' reverses RED to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a central European river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: 8 working on NHS, getting ahead

indicators.note: the letters are put to work in a different order, an anagram signal

explanation.surface: Working for the National Health Service helps you get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' joins the fodder: ON, NHS and AHEAD are rearranged together. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shenandoah is a river in Virginia and West Virginia, famous from the folk song.

clue.text: Most of us have at least one bluff relation

definitions.text: Most of us have at least one

parts.note: a bluff is a steep cliff or bank, as by a river
a relation is a telling or narrative, an account

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone has a relative who tries a bluff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff relation' reads as a blustering relative, but bluff is a steep bank and relation is a telling. The definition is deliberately vague.
explanation.definitionFit: Most adults keep money with a bank, so nearly everyone holds a current or savings arrangement of this kind.

clue.text: State rescue vessel comes back to a massive explosion

indicators.note: something that comes back travels in reverse, so the two pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: AK is the postal abbreviation for Alaska, a US state
Noah's ark rescued the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A state's lifeboat returns to the scene of a huge blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back' turns AK and ARK together into KRAKA, then 'to a' is added as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1883 eruption of the Indonesian volcano on this island was one of the loudest blasts ever recorded.

clue.text: Old lady has money for Indian food

parts.note: nan is an informal word for a grandmother
bread is slang for money

explanation.surface: Grandma pays out cash for a curry dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened flatbread baked in a tandoor and served with curries in South Asian cooking.

clue.text: 8 reported beer after school

indicators.note: in the answer this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the word is taken by how it sounds

parts.note: the drink's name said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have had a beer after school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' signals a sound-alike: BEER spoken without the R gives BIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gambia is the West African river that gives its name to the country along its banks.

clue.text: 8 25% reduction of electric power to audio visual aid

indicators.note: a reduction of the word cuts it down, so a letter is dropped from it

parts.note: a volt is a unit of electric potential, loosely called power
a quarter of the four letters of the word for electric power is a single letter, here its second
AVA is short for audio-visual aid: AV plus A for aid

explanation.surface: Cutting the voltage by a quarter for a classroom projector.
explanation.walkthrough: '25% reduction of' removes one of the four letters of VOLT, the O, leaving VLT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vltava is the Czech river through Prague, celebrated in Smetana's tone poem.

clue.text: 8 instrument approached afresh — just one of five!

indicators.note: the instrument is approached anew, with a new letter at its front

parts.note: the banjo is a stringed instrument
a quin is one of quintuplets, so just one is a quin

explanation.surface: An instrument is tackled anew: only one of five can play it.
explanation.walkthrough: BANJO has its first letter replaced by S; the clue does not say which letter to use, so crossings must supply it.
explanation.definitionFit: The San Joaquin is a river of California's Central Valley, flowing into San Francisco Bay.

clue.text: 8 needs to begin joint, otherwise he was desperate

indicators.note: to begin a word is its first letter

parts.note: or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or we'll be late'
Desperate Dan is a strong-man cowboy in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A man needed to roll a joint first, or else he was desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a long-running character in The Dandy, a British children's comic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jordan is the Middle Eastern river flowing into the Dead Sea, where Jesus was baptised.

clue.text: African dictator involved in no good calling

indicators.note: being involved in something puts one inside it

parts.note: Idi Amin ruled Uganda in the 1970s

explanation.surface: An African dictator caught up in no good vocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'calling' looks like a noun for a vocation; it is the verb sense of giving a name to.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling a child something means giving it a name, so the two participles are synonyms.

clue.text: 8 cockney fixer

indicators.note: a cockney speaker turns the vowel of 'nail' into one rhyming with 'mile', so the word is said aloud that way

parts.note: a nail fixes things together

explanation.surface: A river, a fixer from London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class Londoner; in cockney speech 'nail' sounds like the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great river of Egypt, often called the longest in the world.

clue.text: Dispersed in Serbia, now residents elsewhere in Europe

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Scattered across Serbia, with other people now living elsewhere on the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now' is a link word joining wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaniards and Portuguese live on the Iberian peninsula, in the far west of the continent.

clue.text: 8 drink to be served up not even ready

indicators.note: served up is read as turned up, so the word is reversed

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink

indicators.note: not the even letters means the odd ones, first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A drink is about to be served, though it is not quite ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be served up' reverses RUM; 'not even' takes the odd letters of READY, R, A, Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The Murray is Australia's longest river, flowing through New South Wales, Victoria and South Australia.

clue.text: 8 index in article by the Scotsman

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: mon is a Scots form of 'man'
an A to Z is a street index or alphabetical guide

explanation.surface: An index appears in an article written by the Scottish newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Scotsman' suggests the Edinburgh newspaper, but it gives MON, Scots for man. An A-Z is a British street atlas with an index.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is South America's mightiest river, carrying more water than any other.

clue.text: 8 one departing from Niagara Falls

indicators.note: falls means tumbles about, so the letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A river with someone leaving from Niagara Falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one departing from' takes I out of NIAGARA; 'Falls' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angara is a Siberian river that drains Lake Baikal, a tributary of the Yenisei.
